name: Shellac
label: Touch and Go
lede: The most famous recording engineer in rock spent thirty-two years in a trio that answered hecklers mid-set, played the festivals it said it hated, and put out its last album ten days after he died.

eras.title: An informal collaboration
eras.text: After Big Black and Rapeman, Steve Albini started playing with drummer Todd Trainer with no plan beyond the next practice. Two singles and a debut album later, Shellac had the sound it would keep for thirty years: dry, loud, angular and funny.

years.h: Steve Albini and Todd Trainer start Shellac in Chicago
years.p: Shellac begins as an informal collaboration between Steve Albini and drummer [[Todd Trainer|6c123659-4d26-487f-b156-6b56ffa2bc4c]] of [[Breaking Circus|5f92a6ee-44ef-4eef-8b5b-1bd359b32fd4]], [[Rifle Sport|54f70716-5cef-43e0-99c1-d91b5bd518b4]] and [[Brick Layer Cake|0e15affb-9c59-4c63-99f0-72e44b92c315]]. Ex-[[Naked Raygun|85d2e30c-92fd-4c7f-a2dc-f988a70e234d]] bassist Camilo Gonzalez sits in on early practices.

years.h: Bob Weston of Volcano Suns joins on bass
years.p: Camilo Gonzalez plays on one song on Shellac's first single, then [[Bob Weston|7364260a-0a3e-4a6c-bcf8-b4e743c0b2c0]] of Boston's [[Volcano Suns|4837e8d3-a13f-4670-9684-82970411f4bc]] joins for good. The Albini, Trainer and Weston line-up never changes.

years.h: Shellac's first singles on Touch and Go
years.p: Touch and Go releases a pair of Shellac 7" singles, the start of a relationship that lasts the band's whole life.
Shellac's guitarist engineers [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]]'s third album. It fixes his public reputation, though he always preferred "recording engineer" to "producer."

years.src: Wikipedia: At Action Park · Wikipedia: Shellac
years.h: At Action Park, Shellac's debut album · Touch and Go
years.p: Recorded in March 1994 at Southern in London and Black Box in Noyant-la-Gravoyère, France. The hand-assembled sleeve carries a made-up map of Action Park and an old medical text on electric-shock resuscitation.
years.xp: Albini's sound came from copper picks, Travis Bean aluminum-neck guitars and a Harmonic Percolator distortion pedal, over Weston's bass and Trainer's huge, spare drumming. Fact ranked it the 18th best album of the 1990s in 2012.

eras.title: Records on their own clock
eras.text: Albini opened his own studio and Shellac kept a pace no label would allow: a record when they felt like it, shows when they chose. When Shellac played festivals, it was on its own terms.

years.p: Shellac's second album, three years after At Action Park.

years.h: Steve Albini opens Electrical Audio in Chicago
years.p: Albini founds Electrical Audio, a Chicago studio built to record bands live and cheaply.
Shellac's third album, a year after The Futurist.
Shellac's fourth album, and the last for seven years.

years.h: Shellac curates All Tomorrow's Parties at Camber Sands
years.p: The band that avoided festivals curates ATP at an English holiday camp. Wikipedia says [[Mogwai|d700b3f5-45af-4d02-95ed-57d301bda93e]] had talked Albini into playing ATP, and Shellac became its house band.
years.xp: To mark their 20th anniversary, Shellac curated ATP again in December 2012.

eras.title: Any questions?
eras.text: Shellac settled into a rhythm: an album every seven years, a yearly trip to Barcelona, and a set that stopped halfway so the band could argue with the crowd.

years.h: Shellac's mid-set Q&A, and a standing Primavera date
years.p: Shellac plays Primavera Sound in Barcelona, and returns every year after except 2007. At many shows the band stops mid-set to take questions shouted from fans and hecklers.
years.xp: Wikipedia describes the answers as off-the-cuff and at times jocular. The Q&A became as much a part of a Shellac show as the songs.

years.p: Shellac's first album in seven years.

years.h: Shellac curates ATP again for its 20th anniversary
years.p: Ten years after its first turn, Shellac curates All Tomorrow's Parties a second time to celebrate two decades as a band.
The last Shellac album released in Steve Albini's lifetime.

years.h: The End of Radio: Shellac's John Peel sessions
years.p: Touch and Go collects Shellac's sessions for BBC DJ John Peel.

eras.title: Ten days
eras.text: Shellac announced its first album in a decade in spring 2024. Steve Albini died ten days before it came out.

years.h: Steve Albini dies of a heart attack at 61
years.p: Steve Albini dies of a heart attack at his home in Chicago on May 7, 2024. Shellac's line-up had never changed in 32 years.

years.h: To All Trains arrives ten days later
years.p: Shellac's seventh album, on Touch and Go, comes out ten days after Steve Albini's death.

eras.title: Steve Albini Way
eras.text: With Albini gone, Shellac was over. The tributes came from the places the band had made its own.

years.h: Primavera Sound holds a listening party in Shellac's slot
years.p: Primavera Sound, where Shellac played nearly every year since 2006, plays To All Trains during the band's scheduled set and names a stage after Albini.

years.h: Chicago names Steve Albini Way outside Electrical Audio
years.p: The stretch of Belmont Avenue in Chicago where Electrical Audio stands gets the honorary name Steve Albini Way.
